18	The bulk of Plaintiffs’ breach claim centers around their argument that TD’s conduct violated the NACHA Rules, which Plaintiffs claim were incorporated into the Account Agreement. See Compl. at ¶ 166-67. In order to address this claim we must first determine whether the NACHA rules were in fact incorporated. In support of this point, Plaintiffs cite to page 16 of the Account Agreement, which states in relevant part:
19	International ACH and Wire Transactions
20	If your Account receives incoming ACH transactions (either credits or debits) or wire transfers initiated from outside of the United States, both you and we are subject to the Operating Rules and Guidelines of the National Automated Clearing House Association (“NACHA”) or the rules of any wire transfer system involved....
21	As TD points out, this provision does not refer to all ACH transactions, but rather only to those initiated from outside of the United States. Motion to Dismiss at 18 (Doc. No. 23). Thus to the extent that an ACH transaction was initiated within the United States, we see nothing in the Account Agreement that would obligate TD to follow the NACHA rules for processing that transaction.

{"judgments": [
{"clause_id":"c001","reasoning_cat1":"A short insuring promise to pay proceeds 'according to the following provisions'; the operative words are generic and heavily OCR-degraded but carry no genuinely competing meaning on their face.","reasoning_cat2":"It defers wholly to Sections 4 and 5, and I found no operative provision it contradicts, though it is the hook by which any proceeds dispute (4.1, 5.10) is framed.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.08},
{"clause_id":"c002","reasoning_cat1":"Standard free-look language; 'within 20 days after you receive it' is a definite period, and the garbling is transcription rather than drafting.","reasoning_cat2":"Nothing in Section 3 (premium payment) or 7.2 (effective date) contradicts a refund on return within 20 days.","prob_cat1":0.09,"prob_cat2":0.06},
{"clause_id":"c003","reasoning_cat1":"'Paid-up for level life insurance' with a death benefit 'level amount based on the current Policy Account Value less any Policy Indebtedness' is incomplete and its measure of benefit is genuinely uncertain.","reasoning_cat2":"It sits awkwardly against Section 4.2's Coverage Option A/B death-benefit formulas and the Specified Amount, since after age 95 the benefit would apparently be account-value based rather than the Specified Amount.","prob_cat1":0.31,"prob_cat2":0.34},
{"clause_id":"c004","reasoning_cat1":"A definitional preamble stating that Sections 3-10 give a 'more complete description'; it creates no operative right and names no ambiguous term.","reasoning_cat2":"It functions as an interpretive priority rule subordinating Section 2 definitions to later sections, which could matter if a definition (e.g. 2.15's cross-reference) conflicts with the operative text.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.16},
{"clause_id":"c005","reasoning_cat1":"Simple identification of the Insured as the person whose death causes proceeds to be paid; no competing reading.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 4.1 and Section 1's designation of Ms. Antonio as both Owner and Insured.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c006","reasoning_cat1":"Definition of 'you' as the Owner, expressly allowing Owner and Insured to differ; unambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"Fits Section 8.1-8.2 on ownership and change of ownership without tension.","prob_cat1":0.05,"prob_cat2":0.05},
{"clause_id":"c007","reasoning_cat1":"Pure party identification of the insurer; nothing to construe.","reasoning_cat2":"No other provision uses 'we' differently.","prob_cat1":0.04,"prob_cat2":0.04},
{"clause_id":"c008","reasoning_cat1":"Truncated definition ('as named in the original application but may subsequently be changed'); the change mechanism is not stated here, but the term itself is not ambiguous.","reasoning_cat2":"It depends entirely on Section 8.4, which adds that the Owner is beneficiary if none is named — a gap in 2.4 rather than a conflict.","prob_cat1":0.11,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c009","reasoning_cat1":"'The total amount we are obligated to pay' on death or on surrender; the phrase 'while this Policy is in force and the Insured is alive' is oddly placed but the sense is recoverable.","reasoning_cat2":"Squares with 4.1 (Surrender Value if living, Death Proceeds if not) and 5.7; I found no clause defining Proceeds differently.","prob_cat1":0.13,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c010","reasoning_cat1":"Definite computational anchor date shown in Section 1; nothing vague.","reasoning_cat2":"Used consistently by 2.17 (Monthly Due Date) and 7.2 (Effective Date); the Section 1 specifications page is largely illegible, which is an evidentiary rather than construction problem.","prob_cat1":0.06,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c011","reasoning_cat1":"'The date coverage commences' is a one-line definition that simply cross-refers elsewhere; little to construe in itself.","reasoning_cat2":"It points to Section 7.2 for the initial policy, while 3.1 says there is 'no insurance coverage in effect until the payment is made' — three provisions on when coverage starts that must be harmonised.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.24},
{"clause_id":"c012","reasoning_cat1":"A stranded fragment ('age on the birthday nearest the first...'); as written it does not state a complete rule, though the standard nearest-birthday convention is recoverable.","reasoning_cat2":"Age drives the 5.4 cost-of-insurance table and the 4.2 corridor percentages, so an incomplete age definition could unsettle both.","prob_cat1":0.20,"prob_cat2":0.17},
{"clause_id":"c013","reasoning_cat1":"'The Planned Periodic Premium ... is the minimum that must be paid' during the first two years sits beside the statement that payments may exceed the amount 'required at any time'; what is 'required' is not clearly fixed.","reasoning_cat2":"It must be read with 3.2(1)-(2) and the 5.10 no-lapse test, which measure the first-two-year obligation differently (a running one-twelfth-per-month test rather than a flat minimum).","prob_cat1":0.24,"prob_cat2":0.28},
{"clause_id":"c014","reasoning_cat1":"A single-sentence definition tying the Minimum Initial Premium to a Section 1 figure; definite.","reasoning_cat2":"Consistent with 3.1 and 7.2, both of which condition coverage on its payment.","prob_cat1":0.08,"prob_cat2":0.09},
{"clause_id":"c015","reasoning_cat1":"Badly truncated ('the amount you specified in the original application ... used in determining the amount of death benefit'), but the concept is standard.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 6.2 supplies the increase/decrease mechanism it cross-refers to; no contradiction located.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.10},
{"clause_id":"c016","reasoning_cat1":"Definition of Death Benefit 'prior to any adjustment specified in Section 4'; the reference to unspecified adjustments is broad but Section 4 supplies them.","reasoning_cat2":"Section 4.2 both computes and then adjusts (riders up, indebtedness down), so the definition and operative text can be harmonised.","prob_cat1":0.14,"prob_cat2":0.13},
{"clause_id":"c017","reasoning_cat1":"'An increased death benefit when the difference between the Policy Account Value and the death benefit reaches a minimum size' uses the undefined and vague phrase 'minimum size'.","reasoning_cat2":"The corridor is actually implemented by the age-percentage table in 4.2, so the definition's vague formulation is cured only by reading the later section.","prob_cat1":0.32,"prob_cat2":0.22},
{"clause_id":"c018","reasoning_cat1":"The definition is clear in substance but closes with 'See Section 4.3', a mis-citation: the Monthly Insurance Charge is Section 5.3 and 4.3 is interest on death proceeds.","reasoning_cat2":"That wrong cross-reference is a defect in the provision's relationship to Sections 4.3 and 5.3, though the correct target is obvious enough to be harmonised.","prob_cat1":0.34,"prob_cat2":0.29},
{"clause_id":"c019","reasoning_cat1":"'The charge we make for providing pure insurance protection using the current Cost of Insurance rates' is definite in form, though 'current' rates are set by the insurer.","reasoning_cat2":"The cross-reference to 5.4 is correct and 5.4 supplies the formula and guaranteed maximums; no conflict found.","prob_cat1":0.15,"prob_cat2":0.11},
{"clause_id":"c020","reasoning_cat1":"'The same day of each month as shown in the Policy Date' is a mechanical rule with no competing reading.","reasoning_cat2":"Used identically in 5.3, 5.10 and 9.2; consistent throughout.","prob_cat1":0.07,"prob_cat2":0.06},
